title: Bear and Reverse Radewoosh
statementMd:
Limak and Radewoosh are going to compete against each other in the upcoming algorithmic contest. They are equally skilled but they won't solve problems in the same order.

There will be $*n*$ problems. The $*i*$-th problem has initial score $*p*_{*i*}$ and it takes exactly $*t*_{*i*}$ minutes to solve it. Problems are sorted by difficulty — it's guaranteed that $*p*_{*i*} < *p*_{*i* + 1}$ and $*t*_{*i*} < *t*_{*i* + 1}$.

A constant $*c*$ is given too, representing the speed of loosing points. Then, submitting the $*i*$-th problem at time $*x*$ ($*x*$ minutes after the start of the contest) gives $*max*(0,  *p*_{*i*} - *c*·*x*)$ points.

Limak is going to solve problems in order $1, 2, ..., *n*$ (sorted increasingly by $*p*_{*i*}$). Radewoosh is going to solve them in order $*n*, *n* - 1, ..., 1$ (sorted decreasingly by $*p*_{*i*}$). Your task is to predict the outcome — print the name of the winner (person who gets more points at the end) or a word "`Tie`" in case of a tie.

You may assume that the duration of the competition is greater or equal than the sum of all $*t*_{*i*}$. That means both Limak and Radewoosh will accept all $*n*$ problems.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $*n*$ and $*c*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 50, 1 ≤ *c* ≤ 1000$) — the number of problems and the constant representing the speed of loosing points.

The second line contains $*n*$ integers $*p*_{1}, *p*_{2}, ..., *p*_{*n*}$ ($1 ≤ *p*_{*i*} ≤ 1000, *p*_{*i*} < *p*_{*i* + 1}$) — initial scores.

The third line contains $*n*$ integers $*t*_{1}, *t*_{2}, ..., *t*_{*n*}$ ($1 ≤ *t*_{*i*} ≤ 1000, *t*_{*i*} < *t*_{*i* + 1}$) where $*t*_{*i*}$ denotes the number of minutes one needs to solve the $*i*$-th problem.

## Output

Print "`Limak`" (without quotes) if Limak will get more points in total. Print "`Radewoosh`" (without quotes) if Radewoosh will get more points in total. Print "`Tie`" (without quotes) if Limak and Radewoosh will get the same total number of points.

## Note

In the first sample, there are $3$ problems. Limak solves them as follows:

1. Limak spends $10$ minutes on the $1$-st problem and he gets $50 - *c*·10 = 50 - 2·10 = 30$ points.
2. Limak spends $15$ minutes on the $2$-nd problem so he submits it $10 + 15 = 25$ minutes after the start of the contest. For the $2$-nd problem he gets $85 - 2·25 = 35$ points.
3. He spends $25$ minutes on the $3$-rd problem so he submits it $10 + 15 + 25 = 50$ minutes after the start. For this problem he gets $250 - 2·50 = 150$ points.

So, Limak got $30 + 35 + 150 = 215$ points.

Radewoosh solves problem in the reversed order:

1. Radewoosh solves $3$-rd problem after $25$ minutes so he gets $250 - 2·25 = 200$ points.
2. He spends $15$ minutes on the $2$-nd problem so he submits it $25 + 15 = 40$ minutes after the start. He gets $85 - 2·40 = 5$ points for this problem.
3. He spends $10$ minutes on the $1$-st problem so he submits it $25 + 15 + 10 = 50$ minutes after the start. He gets $*max*(0, 50 - 2·50) = *max*(0, - 50) = 0$ points.

Radewoosh got $200 + 5 + 0 = 205$ points in total. Limak has $215$ points so Limak wins.

In the second sample, Limak will get $0$ points for each problem and Radewoosh will first solve the hardest problem and he will get $250 - 6·25 = 100$ points for that. Radewoosh will get $0$ points for other two problems but he is the winner anyway.

In the third sample, Limak will get $2$ points for the $1$-st problem and $2$ points for the $2$-nd problem. Radewoosh will get $4$ points for the $8$-th problem. They won't get points for other problems and thus there is a tie because $2 + 2 = 4$.
statementZhMd:
Limak 和 Radewoosh 将在即将到来的算法竞赛中展开竞争。他们的实力相当，但解题顺序不同。

比赛中将有 $*n*$ 道题。第 $*i*$ 道题的初始分数为 $*p*_{*i*}$，需要恰好 $*t*_{*i*}$ 分钟才能解出。题目按难度排序——保证 $*p*_{*i*} < *p*_{*i* + 1}$ 且 $*t*_{*i*} < *t*_{*i* + 1}$。

另给定一个常数 $*c*$，表示分数随时间降低的速度。在时间 $*x*$ 提交第 $*i*$ 道题（即比赛开始后 $*x*$ 分钟）可获得 $*max*(0,  *p*_{*i*} - *c*·*x*)$ 分。

Limak 将按照 $1, 2, ..., *n*$ 的顺序解题（即按 $*p*_{*i*}$ 递增的顺序）。Radewoosh 将按照 $*n*, *n* - 1, ..., 1$ 的顺序解题（即按 $*p*_{*i*}$ 递减的顺序）。你的任务是预测比赛结果——输出最终获得分数更多者的姓名；如果双方得分相同，则输出单词 "`Tie`"。

可以认为比赛时长大于等于所有 $*t*_{*i*}$ 之和。这意味着 Limak 和 Radewoosh 都会提交全部 $*n*$ 道题。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*c*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 50, 1 ≤ *c* ≤ 1000$）——题目数量以及表示分数降低速度的常数。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*p*_{1}, *p*_{2}, ..., *p*_{*n*}$（$1 ≤ *p*_{*i*} ≤ 1000, *p*_{*i*} < *p*_{*i* + 1}$）——各题的初始分数。

第三行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*t*_{1}, *t*_{2}, ..., *t*_{*n*}$（$1 ≤ *t*_{*i*} ≤ 1000, *t*_{*i*} < *t*_{*i* + 1}$），其中 $*t*_{*i*}$ 表示解出第 $*i*$ 道题所需的分钟数。

## 输出格式

如果 Limak 获得的总分更高，输出 "`Limak`"（不含引号）。

如果 Radewoosh 获得的总分更高，输出 "`Radewoosh`"（不含引号）。

如果 Limak 和 Radewoosh 获得的总分相同，输出 "`Tie`"（不含引号）。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，共有 $3$ 道题。Limak 的解题过程如下：

1. Limak 花费 $10$ 分钟解决第 $1$ 道题，获得 $50 - *c*·10 = 50 - 2·10 = 30$ 分。
2. Limak 花费 $15$ 分钟解决第 $2$ 道题，因此他在比赛开始 $10 + 15 = 25$ 分钟后提交。对于第 $2$ 道题，他获得 $85 - 2·25 = 35$ 分。
3. 他花费 $25$ 分钟解决第 $3$ 道题，因此他在比赛开始 $10 + 15 + 25 = 50$ 分钟后提交。对于这道题，他获得 $250 - 2·50 = 150$ 分。

因此，Limak 获得了 $30 + 35 + 150 = 215$ 分。

Radewoosh 按相反的顺序解题：

1. Radewoosh 在 $25$ 分钟后解决第 $3$ 道题，因此获得 $250 - 2·25 = 200$ 分。
2. 他花费 $15$ 分钟解决第 $2$ 道题，因此在比赛开始 $25 + 15 = 40$ 分钟后提交。他获得 $85 - 2·40 = 5$ 分。
3. 他花费 $10$ 分钟解决第 $1$ 道题，因此在比赛开始 $25 + 15 + 10 = 50$ 分钟后提交。他获得 $*max*(0, 50 - 2·50) = *max*(0, - 50) = 0$ 分。

Radewoosh 总共获得了 $200 + 5 + 0 = 205$ 分。Limak 获得了 $215$ 分，因此 Limak 获胜。

在第二个样例中，Limak 每道题都只能获得 $0$ 分，而 Radewoosh 会先解决最难的题，并获得 $250 - 6·25 = 100$ 分。Radewoosh 解决另外两道题时会获得 $0$ 分，但他仍然获胜。

在第三个样例中，Limak 解决第 $1$ 道题和第 $2$ 道题时各获得 $2$ 分。Radewoosh 解决第 $8$ 道题时获得 $4$ 分。他们解决其他题目时都不会获得分数，因此结果为平局，因为 $2 + 2 = 4$。
